new_statements.rule_in_words: In the Mba group (Mba/Kimanga, Ndunga, 'Dongo, Ma) stress -- sometimes with slight lengthening -- falls on the first syllable of the word stem; noun-class suffixes are never stressed. Since Mba stems carry no prefixes apart from a sporadic a-, this amounts to stem-initial (usually word-initial) stress in a two-level tone language.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the statement is hedged ('seems to'). Sec. 1a adds that the vowels I and U recorded by Tucker 'appear to be unstressed forms of' open e and o.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement about the stem within the word (class suffixes excluded from stress); given for the MBA Group as a whole, based on Tucker & Hackett's own L.S.N.B.B. field notes on Mba plus Carrington 1949 (Mba) and de Boeck 1952 (Ndunga). All Mba-specific descriptions (Bokula 1971, 1982; Fiedler et al. 2021) describe tone only and are silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is made for Tucker & Bryan's 'MBA Group' collectively (Mba/Kimanga mbaa1245, Ndunga ndun1249, 'Dongo dong1292, Ma/Amadi mayo? = maaa1234), not for Mba alone, though Mba is the group's reference language and Tucker's own field notes were on Mba. All Mba-specific sources opened (Bokula 1971, 1980, 1982, 1983; Fiedler et al. 2021) treat Mba as a tone language (H/L lexically, plus a mid level per Bokula) and say nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Bokula Moiso. 1982. Etude comparee des langues ndunga et mba (Zaire). Annales Aequatoria 3: 107-129.
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sec. 1.10 'La tonalite' (pp. 119-120): Mba has three simple tones (haut, moyen, bas), isolation words rest on H and L, mid tone mostly in connected speech; 'Les tons sont generalement fixes'. No accent/stress statement; syllables all open (1.6).

sources.citation: Bokula Moiso. 1980. Les predicats non-verbaux en mba. Annales Aequatoria 1 (Tome I, part II): 505-527.
sources.note: Generative-semantic syntax article; no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bokula, F.-X. [Moiso]. 1971. Formes nominales et pronominales en mba. Africana Linguistica 5: 41-77. Tervuren: MRAC. doi 10.3406/aflin.1971.884
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 2 'La tonalite' (pp. 54-58): 'Le mba est une langue tonale. Seules les voyelles portent les tons' with three pitch levels (haut, moyen, bas), isolation forms resting on H vs L; tone types of nouns by syllable count; no mention of accent d'intensite.
